grade_6.course_name: Learn and Grow - Year 6 Basic Education
key_grammar_topics: Prepositions of place (in, on, at, under, next to)
main_modules: Entertaining Myself - Leisure activities, making suggestions
Keeping Fit - Health, food, giving advice
Having Fun in the Seasons - Weather, seasons, comparatives
Caring - Helping others, jobs, superlatives
Celebrations - Past events, celebrations
Going Shopping - Shops, clothes, shopping dialogues
Around the World - Countries, transport, customs
writing_types: Simple paragraph about self or family
common_errors: Forgetting 's' in third person singular (he go → he goes)
Confusing 'to be' with other verbs (I am like → I like)
Missing auxiliary in questions (You like? → Do you like?)
Double negatives (I don't like nothing → I don't like anything)
Incorrect word order in questions
Confusing 'his' and 'her'
Using infinitive instead of gerund (I like play → I like playing)
grade_6.encouragement_style: Very enthusiastic, use simple praise like 'Great job!', 'Well done!', 'You're doing great!'

grade_7.course_name: Let's Learn English - 7th Year Basic Education
key_grammar_topics: Future forms: will, going to, present continuous for future
Modal verbs: can, could, may, might, must, should, have to
Relative pronouns: who, which, that, where
main_modules: Tell Me About Yourself - Family, hobbies, routines
My Immediate Environment - Friends, food, preferences
My Home and City - House, market, celebrations
Health and Safety - Safety rules, health, weather
School Life - Facilities, teachers, responsibilities
common_errors: Confusing past simple and present perfect (I have seen him yesterday → I saw him yesterday)
Incorrect present perfect formation (I have go → I have gone)
Using past simple in present perfect context
Forgetting 'to be' in passive voice (The book write → The book is written)
Confusing 'for' and 'since' with present perfect
Incorrect question formation with modals
Misusing relative pronouns (The man which → The man who)
grade_7.encouragement_style: Positive and supportive, acknowledge progress: 'You're making great progress!', 'I can see you're thinking about this!', 'Good effort!'

key_grammar_topics: Third Conditional (If + past perfect, would have + past participle)
Modal verbs for deduction (must, might, can't, could)
main_modules: Tell Me About Yourself and Your Plans
School and Education
Holidays and Leisure
Travel and Tourism
Relationships
common_errors: Confusing present perfect and present perfect continuous
Incorrect sequence of tenses in reported speech
Forgetting to change time expressions in reported speech
Passive voice word order errors
Confusing second and third conditionals
Incorrect use of relative pronouns in non-defining clauses
Missing commas in non-defining relative clauses
Confusing 'say' and 'tell' in reported speech
grade_8.encouragement_style: Professional yet warm, acknowledge complexity: 'This is challenging, but you're handling it well!', 'Excellent thinking!', 'You're developing strong skills!'

grade_9.course_name: Proceed with English - 9th Year Basic Education
key_grammar_topics: All conditional forms (zero, first, second, third, mixed)
Modal perfects (must have, should have, could have)
Advanced linking words and discourse markers
Subjunctive mood (I suggest that he go)
main_modules: Family Life - Family relationships, responsibilities, conflict resolution
Education - Learning styles, study skills, educational systems
Health and Environment - Healthy lifestyle, environmental issues
Services - Public services, consumer rights, complaints
Entertainment - Media, arts, sports, leisure
Civility - Citizenship, rights and duties, volunteering
common_errors: Mixing conditional types (If I would have...)
Incorrect modal perfect formation
Passive voice with incorrect agent
Confusing gerunds and infinitives (I avoided to go → I avoided going)
Incorrect participle clause construction
Overuse of passive voice
Comma splices in complex sentences
Incorrect inversion structures
Misplaced modifiers
Subject-verb agreement in complex sentences
grade_9.encouragement_style: Mature and respectful, recognize sophistication: 'Your analysis shows deep understanding!', 'Excellent critical thinking!', 'You're ready for advanced work!'
